caption: We financed the inverter through the installer just to get the lights back on and never checked the rate. Did load shedding get you into a loan you didn't plan for either?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R28 000
household income
Living in Lichtenburg
slides.body:
Him 36, her 33
Married, two kids
Jobs: Irrigation technician & co-op till supervisor
Combined net: R28 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bedroom on the edge of town
slides.body: The one number that hasn't moved in five years, rates aside.

slides.title: Inverter & solar loan
slides.includes: Financed through the installer during the worst of load shedding, 41 months left
slides.body: We didn't shop around, we just wanted the lights back on. We're still paying for that decision.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of four, one big monthly shop plus top-ups
slides.body: Two kids at the age where the trolley fills up faster than the payslip does.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: The one car between us, does both jobs and the school run
slides.body: It has to work for two households' worth of errands, and there's no backup if it doesn't.

slides.title: School fees & stationery
slides.body: The stationery list gets longer every single year and nobody explains why.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, car insurance, cellphone & data, two funeral policies, stokvel, prepaid electricity
slides.body: Six things between us that we'd never once added up together until now.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R28 000 combined. Split two ways, that's not the cushion either of us thought a double income would buy.

slides.title: We finally saw the solar loan next to everything else
slides.body:
We imported both our statements into Beyond Horizon and saw the inverter instalment sitting right next to the bond for the first time. It's not the villain we expected, but it's not nothing either.

No bank login needed.
